title: Justin Welsh on running a ~$15M one-person business and what to sell in the AI era
summary: Justin Welsh breaks down his revenue mix (courses, newsletter sponsorships, partnerships, membership), how AI commoditization forced him to rethink his model, and why he's betting on authentic writing and proximity. He also covers choosing a medium, using AI as an editor, storytelling over how-tos, and bootstrapping.

principles.text: Pick the medium you love and get excellent at it; the best channel is that medium, not a platform.
principles.quote: the most valuable channel is whatever medium you become excellent at. So there are only so many mediums. There's video, there's audio, there's writing.

principles.text: Don't use a platform you dislike just because it has reach; try mediums and keep the one you enjoy.
principles.quote: going on a platform and doing something you dislike simply because it has reach the definition of a bad life to me.

principles.text: As AI commoditizes information and products, monetize proximity and authentic writing instead.
principles.quote: One one thing that you can sell is you can lean heavily into AI. It's just not me.

principles.text: Use AI as an editor and thought partner after writing yourself, so you keep your own writing skill.
principles.quote: I can write my stuff and then I can push it through an AI and say like where are the gaps?

principles.text: Distribution is an accelerant, not a must-have; tell a unique story and be someone people want to follow.
principles.quote: I think it's an accelerant, not a must-have.

principles.text: Prefer bootstrapping and compounding small wins over big moonshots; keep margins high and ask how much you need.
principles.quote: I'd rather have 10 wins and have two of them eventually not be wins and have eight wins left over than take a moonshot and be left with nothing.
